proof_summary: Successive binomial coefficients are factored into products \(F_c=\prod_{p\nmid i}(1+c p^r/i)\) for \(c=1,2\); pairing \(i\) with \(p^r-i\) and expanding through the second elementary symmetric term reduces the needed valuation to reciprocal power-sum divisibilities obtained from inversion and Faulhaber formulas. An inductively established auxiliary divisibility \(p^3\mid 2\binom{3p^{r-1}}{p^{r-1}}^2-9\binom{2p^{r-1}}{p^{r-1}}\) supplies the remaining powers of \(p\), after which a factor congruent to \(2\pmod p\) is canceled.
